newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin says serious questions over 1997 budget.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin says serious questions over 1997 budget.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin said on Friday he had "major doubts" that the government's 1997 budget, which he signed earlier this week, could be fulfilled.
But in a brief radio address he said he had signed it reluctantly to avoid aggravating political tensions.
"There are very major doubts that the budget is capable of being fulfilled," the 66-year-old Kremlin leader said in his second radio broadcast since recovering from pneumonia.

"I will tell you straight away that such a decision (signing the budget) did not come easily to me. There are major doubts about many key items," Yeltsin said, faulting the government for not working hard enough on the document.

He said the budget law contained a host of "unrealistic articles" and that the oppposition-dominated State Duma lower house of parliament had engaged in populism, damaging the budget further with its amendments.

Refering to Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin, who Russian media have speculated could lose his job, Yeltsin said the premier had promised to meet payment plans for the millions of Russians still owed pensions and wages after months of backlogs.
